cases.question: Which button swings the sword?
cases.answer: The A button swings the sword. (Controls: NES A - Swing the sword.)

cases.question: How much does the Blue Candle cost?
cases.answer: The Blue Candle costs 60 rupees in the documents: it can be purchased for 60 Rupees through a door one screen west of the Fairy Fountain route, and also for 60 rupees in a 2nd Quest shop in Hyrule section 8 (E-4). The walkthrough also mentions earning 60 rupees to purchase it.

cases.question: How many Heart Containers do I need to get the White Sword?
cases.answer: You need five Heart Containers to receive the White Sword, according to the Items document. The Overworld Quest 1 document says six heart containers are needed in one cave, and the Hyrule 3 documents also say at least 5 Heart Containers.

cases.question: Which item can I find in Level-3 of the first quest?
cases.answer: In Level 3 of the first quest, you can find the Raft (it is down the stairwell in the room reached from the compass room). The same dungeon's objectives also list the third Piece of Triforce and a Heart Container.

cases.question: How powerful is the Magic Sword?
cases.answer: The Magic Sword has Damage 4, making it four times as powerful as the wooden sword and the most powerful sword in the game. It requires twelve Heart Containers to receive.

cases.question: How can I sail across the sea?
cases.answer: The raft allows Link to cross lakes and oceans, but it can only be used at a Dock; neither of the 'double docks' trigger raft use.

cases.question: Is there somewhere my hearts get refilled without paying?
cases.answer: Yes. Fairy enemy drops fill 3 of Link's hearts, and in the fairy ponds a fairy fills all of your heart meters.

cases.question: How can I win cash by gambling?
cases.answer: In the Money Making Game, which is found in a cave reached by bombing the cliff wall just left of center in Hyrule 2 section A-5, or by walking into the tree in Hyrule 1 section D-2. Hyrule 6 section C-5 also leads to the Money Making Game via a bombed north wall.

cases.question: What can I buy at D-4 in section 2 of the overworld?
cases.answer: At D-4 in Section 2 (2nd Quest), the shop sells Arrows for 80 rupees, the Magical Shield for 130 rupees, and a set of 4 Bombs for 20 rupees.

cases.question: What happens if I register my name as ZELDA?
cases.answer: Entering your name as "Zelda" at the start of the game immediately begins the Second Quest without playing the First Quest. The documents describe the name as "Zelda"; they do not explicitly confirm that the all-caps form "ZELDA" triggers the same effect.

cases.question: Where can I buy the Blue Candle, and what can it be used for?
cases.answer: You can buy the Blue Candle for 60 Rupees in a shop reached from the Fairy Fountain: walk three screens south then two west (taking the lower path), bomb the rock wall to get 30 Rupees, return to heal, go south two then east four screens, bomb for another 30 Rupees, then go one screen west and enter the door. The Blue Candle throws a flame that can light dark dungeon rooms, burn bushes in the overworld, and damage enemies, but it can only be used once per screen.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Level-1 in the first quest and how do I defeat him?
cases.answer: The boss of Level 1 in the first quest is Aquamentus. You must strike his head six times with the Wooden Sword or three times with the White Sword, timing strikes between the energy orbs he emits from his horn. Only the Magical Shield absorbs the orbs, and sword beams can hit any part of his body.

cases.question: What do I need to enter Level-4 in the first quest, and which item is inside?
cases.answer: Level 4 of the first quest requires the Raft as a prerequisite. Inside, the objectives include obtaining the Ladder, defeating the two-headed Gleeok, obtaining a Heart Container, and the fourth Piece of Triforce, so the Ladder is one of the items found there.

cases.question: How do I beat the dragon boss?
cases.answer: The dragon boss Aquamentus has 6 HP and shoots fireballs that split in three directions; they can only be blocked by the Magical Shield. It is vulnerable to the Sword and Arrows, and can also be killed by two Bombs.

cases.question: How do I defeat Gleeok?
cases.answer: Each Gleeok head must be stabbed until it flies freely around the room, and the free head is still a threat that cannot be defeated. You must destroy every attached head to beat Gleeok, which earns a Heart Container. The number of heads varies by dungeon, with two-headed, three-headed, and four-headed versions appearing.

cases.question: How can I attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. You can also press the B button to use the subweapon you have assigned.

cases.question: Which button do i have to press to attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword, which is the attack action in the Controls document. B is used for subweapons.

cases.question: How can I atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. Press the B button to use your equipped subweapon.

cases.question: how do i open the menu
cases.answer: Press the Start button to bring up the sub-screen menu, where Link can look at the map, change subweapon, and see inventory. Press Start again to return from the sub-screen to the normal view.

cases.question: can i blow up walls with bombz?
cases.answer: Yes. The bomb can be used to blast holes in weak walls, according to the Bomb item description. Several walkthrough entries also say to bomb cliff walls or room walls to reveal hidden passages.

cases.question: how do i use my secondary item
cases.answer: Press the B button to use your secondary item (subweapon). To choose which subweapon is assigned to B, open the sub-screen with Start, then select it with the D-pad, since only one item in the blue box can be assigned to B at a time.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing your sword. You can also press the B button to use your selected subweapon.

cases.question: how can i heal?
cases.answer: Fairy Fountain heals fully: in the fairy ponds a fairy fills all heart meters. Enemy-dropped fairies fill 3 hearts. A medicine woman in the cave at D-4 (Hyrule 1st Quest) sells Red Potions for 68 Rupees or a Water of Life for 40 Rupees, and a Water of Life completely refills your life bar.

cases.question: where do i find money?
cases.answer: Several places in the documents give rupees. The Money Making Game can be played in a cave reached by bombing a rock face immediately left of the start screen (zelda1:cheats:004), or by bombing the north wall in Hyrule 6 section C-5 (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-6:003), or by walking into the tree at Hyrule 1 section D-2 (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-1:003). Other sources include a Red Moblin cave at Hyrule 8 B-4 giving 30 Rupees (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-8:001), and a stairwell at Hyrule 1 B-4 giving 30 Rupees (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-1:003).

cases.question: what is the best weapon?
cases.answer: The most powerful sword in the game is the Magic Sword, which deals 4 damage and is four times as powerful as the Wooden Sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers before he can receive it.

cases.question: how do i open a locked door?
cases.answer: One documented method is to enter the first dungeon, immediately leave, and come back, after which the locked door will open. Keys can also open locked doors, since each Key opens one door.

cases.question: what do i do if ig im stuck
cases.answer: Bomb every wall that does not contain a door, since this often reveals passageways deeper into the dungeon. If a room has no visible way forward, also try pushing blocks after all monsters in the room are defeated, since those can open doors or reveal staircases.

cases.question: how do i defeat the dragon?
cases.answer: The dragon is Gleeok, a multi-headed dragon: Link must attack each head, and when a head takes enough damage it detaches and flies around the room, so dodge its projectiles and focus on the attached heads. Keep stabbing the attached heads until every one is disconnected. The flying heads cannot be damaged directly.

cases.question: where do i get bombs?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, fight and defeat the Moblins in the nearby area until they drop Bombs that you can collect. The Quest 2 overworld list also includes getting some Bombs as a step, but it does not say where. Quest 1 Dungeon 6 mentions replacement Bombs available one screen south-east of the Water of Life woman and then two screens east.

cases.question: how do i unlock the bow?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, Dungeon 1, the Bow is found in room O-1, a room with Traps in each corner and a stairwell in the center surrounded by blocks. The left-most block can be pushed aside to enter the stairwell, where the Bow is located. You'll need to purchase Arrows to use it, unless you already bought them before finding the Bow.

cases.question: how do i save my game?
cases.answer: To save your game, choose "SAVE" on the Game Over screen with Select and press Start; all accomplishments are stored until you next play. You can also use the quick save method: from the sub-screen menu, press Up (D-pad) and A simultaneously on the second controller to access the Save Screen.

cases.question: how do i get more hearts?
cases.answer: You can get a Heart Container, which permanently adds one heart to Link's life meter. The Quest 1 overworld guide describes burning a tree on Lake Hylia to find a fourth Heart Container and using a bomb on a huge rock to get the sixth, and the Quest 2 overworld list includes pushing a tombstone in the Graveyard to get a Heart Container. Fairies also restore hearts, filling 3 of Link's hearts, or all of them in fairy ponds.

cases.question: can i buy a better shield?
cases.answer: Yes. A Magical Shield is sold in several places, such as a shop reached by burning a tree in Quest 1 for 90 Rupees, and it reflects more attacks than the Small Shield Link starts with.

cases.question: how do i see in dark rooms?
cases.answer: You can light dark rooms with a candle: the Blue Candle can be used only once per screen, while the Red Candle has the same effect with no per-screen limit. Candles can light up dark rooms in dungeons.

cases.question: Which button do I press to jump?
cases.answer: Press the A button to jump in the air.

cases.question: How many spirit points does the windmill star cost?
cases.answer: The windmill star costs 5 spirit points to throw.

cases.question: How many lives does Ryu start with?
cases.answer: Ryu starts the game with two lives in reserve.

cases.question: What happens if the clock runs out before I finish a stage?
cases.answer: You lose one life if the timer runs out before you complete a stage.

cases.question: How can I get higher using just one wall?
cases.answer: Use the wall hop technique: jump toward and cling to a wall, hold the jump button, push away from the wall, then immediately push back toward it. If done correctly you rise and cling to the wall higher than where you started, and repeating this can climb to the top of the screen.

cases.question: Who attacks me in Stage 2-3?
cases.answer: In Stage 2-3, you are first attacked by the enemy known as Bomberhead as soon as you enter the hall. Bomberhead's spinning weapon makes it hard to duck below, so you need precise strikes to defeat him.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Stage 3-3?
cases.answer: The boss of Stage 3-3 (Act III) is Basaquer, who leaps back and forth across the room and periodically shoots a trio of darts.

cases.question: What does the fire wheel do and does it use spirit points?
cases.answer: The Fire Wheel surrounds Ryu with a circle of fire that eliminates any enemy that contacts him. It requires no spirit points to use, but it replaces any weapon you currently hold and disappears after five seconds.

cases.question: What is Ninja Gaiden called in Europe?
cases.answer: In Europe, Ninja Gaiden is known as Shadow Warriors.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the B button to attack by swinging your sword, and you can attack low by squatting when you attack. Hold up on the D-pad while pressing B to use a secondary weapon, which requires enough spirit points.

cases.question: how do i get more ninpo?
cases.answer: The documents don't explicitly define "ninpo" or say how to get more of it. They do describe spirit points, which are needed to use secondary weapons: blue tiles give 5 points and red tiles give 10 points. Ninpo is not mentioned, so I can't confirm it is the same resource.

cases.question: how do i heal?
cases.answer: The documents mention health-restoring potions found in lamps, insects, and candles during stages, such as the lamp on the left at the end of the bridge in Stage 4-2 and the insect item in Stage 2-2. Collect these items to restore some lost health. The documents do not describe any other healing method.

cases.question: why did i get sent back to 6-1?
cases.answer: You were likely sent back to 6-1 because you lost to one of the final bosses. According to the Stage 6-3 guide, losing to any of the final bosses returns you all the way to 6-1, regardless of remaining lives. Defeated bosses stay dead, but you do not get a health refill if you need to retry.
